sections.h2: Where is Myrtle Beach and how big is it?
sections.html:
Myrtle Beach is a resort city in Horry County, in northeastern South Carolina, at the center of the roughly 60-mile Grand Strand. It covers 23.69 square miles, almost all of it land, and sits about 94 miles northeast of Charleston and 74 miles southwest of Wilmington, North Carolina.

The city had 35,682 residents in the 2020 census and an estimate of 40,937 for 2025. The median age in 2020 was 49.4, and 25.4 percent of residents were 65 or older. The Intracoastal Waterway has separated the city from the mainland since 1936.

Because the city is small and the visitor count is large, a house here may be a primary home, a retiree's place or a short-term rental, and the tax treatment differs for each.

sections.h2: How did Myrtle Beach get started?
sections.html:
Myrtle Beach began as a lightly settled coastal stretch that became a resort after a railroad arrived in 1900. The Conway and Seashore Railroad was chartered on February 28, 1899 and began daily service on May 1, 1900, and the Seaside Inn opened in 1901.

The Burroughs and Collins Company bought much of the Withers family land in 1881, and a post office named Withers opened in 1888. The name Myrtle Beach honors the southern wax myrtle shrub. The place was incorporated as a town on March 12, 1938 and as a city in 1957. Kings Highway, now U.S. 17, was paved in 1940.

That timeline explains the housing stock: older cottages near the oceanfront, and much newer condos and subdivisions further in. The median build year for the city's homes was 1992 in the data on our page.

sections.h2: What drives the Myrtle Beach economy?
sections.html:
Tourism dominates the Myrtle Beach economy, supported by hotels, restaurants, golf, attractions and retail. The area reports more than 20 million visitors a year, and the city has roughly 425 hotels and between 1,800 and 1,900 restaurants.

  • The Boardwalk opened in 2010 and the 200-foot SkyWheel in May 2011.
  • The Convention Center opened in 2003.
  • Grand Strand Medical Center has 369 beds, and Horry County Schools has about 40,000 students.
  • Myrtle Beach International Airport, three miles southwest of downtown, sits on the former Air Force base that closed in 1993.

The main roads are U.S. 17, U.S. 501, SC 31 and SC 73, and transit comes from Coast RTA. Seasonal work and rental income make cash flow uneven for many owners, and a missed tax payment is easy to fall into during the off-season.

sections.h2: What does the coast mean for a Myrtle Beach house?
sections.html:
Myrtle Beach has a humid subtropical climate with about 53.56 inches of precipitation a year, and hurricanes are the main risk. The worst storm in local history was Hurricane Hazel in 1954, and the most recent significant damage came from Hurricane Hugo in 1989.

Direct hits are rare, and weaker tropical storms are more common. Summer highs run 83 to 91 degrees with lows near 70, and September is the wettest month. Salt air, wind-driven rain and flooding are the issues a buyer's inspector will look at first: roof covering, windows, siding, HVAC and crawl-space moisture.

A house with deferred storm repairs can be hard to finance, and that is one reason owners choose a cash sale. Check your insurance and flood status before listing, since the answers affect what buyers can borrow.

sections.h2: Who bills Myrtle Beach property tax, and where do you pay?
sections.html:
Horry County bills and collects Myrtle Beach property tax; the city does not run its own treasurer's office. The county's real property page says notices go to the owner of record, and city, county and school taxes appear together on the county bill.

The Horry County Treasurer has an office at 332 Hinson Drive in Myrtle Beach, plus offices in Conway, Surfside and Little River:

  • Conway (main): 1301 Second Avenue, Conway, SC 29526
  • Myrtle Beach: 332 Hinson Dr, Myrtle Beach, SC 29579
  • South Strand: 9630 Scipio Lane, Surfside, SC 29588
  • Stephen's Crossroads: 107 Hwy 57 North, Little River, SC 29566

Hours are Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and the main number is (843) 915-5470. Payments may be made in person, by mail, in the night deposit box, online, or by phone at 843-428-2126. Card payments carry convenience fees. For exemptions and address changes on real property, the Tax Assessor is at (843) 915-5040, and the Auditor takes homestead questions at (843) 915-5051.

sections.h2: When is Myrtle Beach property tax due, and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
Payment is due in full on or before January 15 of the year after the tax year, and penalties start on January 16, February 2 and March 17 for payments postmarked later. The county says not receiving a bill does not excuse a penalty.

DatePenalty added (S.C. Code 12-45-180)
January 163 percent
February 27 percent more
March 175 percent more, then tax execution

The county's page does not print percentages, so we took them from the statute. Horry County also has an installment payment program, and the treasurer holds an annual public tax sale for delinquent properties. The sale dates were not on the pages we opened, so ask the Treasurer.

sections.h2: Why do second homes and rentals in Myrtle Beach pay more?
sections.html:
A house that is not a legal residence is assessed at 6 percent of fair market value instead of 4 percent. State law also says a home rented more than 72 days a year does not qualify for the 4 percent ratio.

The City of Myrtle Beach published a news item about a tax calculator, maintained by the Myrtle Beach Area Chamber of Commerce at mbtaxcalc.com. It describes a Tourism Development Fee credit for primary homeowners inside the city. In its example, a $200,000 primary residence paid $127.20 in city property taxes after a $504 credit. That example is for owner-occupied homes only, and the page does not give current millage, so ask the county for your actual figures.

For a seller, the difference can be large. An investor selling a vacation rental and an owner selling a primary home face different bills, and a buyer who plans to live in the house must apply for the 4 percent ratio before the first penalty date.

sections.h2: What if you owe tax and want to sell a Myrtle Beach house?
sections.html:
You can sell, and the title company pays the Horry County balance from your proceeds at closing. Get a payoff from the Treasurer first, because penalties change on January 16, February 2 and March 17.

If a tax sale happens first, S.C. Code 12-51-90 lets the owner redeem within twelve months. The interest is 3 percent of the bid in months one to three, 6 in months four to six, 9 in months seven to nine, and 12 in months ten to twelve.

If you disagree with the value, the written objection goes to the assessor within 90 days after the assessment notice is mailed under S.C. Code 12-60-2510. The Horry County pages we opened did not state an appeal deadline of their own, so call the Assessor at (843) 915-5040 for the form.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Myrtle Beach?
faqs.a: Horry County does. The Treasurer has an office at 332 Hinson Drive in Myrtle Beach and the main office at 1301 Second Avenue in Conway.

faqs.q: When is Myrtle Beach property tax due?
faqs.a: It is due on or before January 15. Penalties start on January 16, then February 2 and March 17.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Myrtle Beach property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes. Horry County accepts online payment by check or Visa, MasterCard or Discover, and card payments carry convenience fees.

faqs.q: What is the Horry County Assessor's phone number?
faqs.a: It is (843) 915-5040, for exemptions, sold property and real property address changes.

faqs.q: Do rentals in Myrtle Beach get the 4 percent rate?
faqs.a: Not if the home is rented more than 72 days a year. State law then treats it as other real property at 6 percent.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Myrtle Beach house with back taxes owed?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is paid from the proceeds at closing, as long as the price covers it. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure.
